messages.content: The client moved Tuesday's first session to 9:00 a.m., so the Tuesday morning flight is out. Monday lodging is approved. Can you put the Monday Delta flight and the Hampton plan together and check the full cost and restrictions before I buy?

Yes. I have the Monday nonstop outbound at 7:05 p.m. from Minneapolis, arriving Raleigh-Durham at 10:38 p.m., and the Friday nonstop return at 5:35 p.m., arriving Minneapolis at 7:24 p.m. The round-trip airfare is $548 including airline taxes.

The hotel is Hampton Inn & Suites Raleigh/Cary-I-40, Monday, October 13 through Friday, October 17, four nights in a standard king at $179 nightly. I will verify the flight fare rules, hotel taxes, cancellation penalty, and timing against the new 9:00 a.m. start.
Good. First, does arriving at 10:38 Monday still leave enough room to get to the hotel and be functional Tuesday morning?

It does, although it will be a late arrival. Allowing about 15 to 25 minutes to exit the aircraft and reach the rideshare area, plus roughly 15 to 25 minutes to Cary at that hour, a reasonable hotel arrival estimate is 11:15 to 11:35 p.m.

For Tuesday, requesting the rideshare around 6:50 a.m. still supports the planned 7:20 office arrival. That gives you more than 90 minutes at the client site before the 9:00 session.
That's fine. What exactly is the $548 Delta fare? I don't want to discover at checkout that it's basic economy.

The selected $548 itinerary is Delta Main Cabin, not Basic Economy. It includes advance standard-seat selection and one carry-on plus one personal item. A checked bag is not included in the quoted price.

The ticket is nonrefundable. Before departure, it can be changed without a separate change fee, but any fare increase applies. If canceled before departure, the value is generally retained as a Delta eCredit rather than returned to the corporate card. The standard 24-hour risk-free cancellation window applies when purchased directly from Delta at least seven days before departure.
No checked bag needed. Are both legs actually nonstop, and are the dates definitely Monday the 13th and Friday the 17th?

Confirmed. Both legs are nonstop:

Monday, October 13: MSP 7:05 p.m. to RDU 10:38 p.m.

Friday, October 17: RDU 5:35 p.m. to MSP 7:24 p.m.

The schedule has no connection or airport change. The $548 total covers the round trip for one traveler in Main Cabin.
Now calculate the hotel with tax, not just the room subtotal.

Four nights at $179 produce a room subtotal of $716. The booking screen applies estimated lodging and sales taxes of $94.87, bringing the hotel total to $810.87.

Adding the $548 airfare gives a combined flight-and-hotel total of $1,358.87. That excludes rideshares, meals beyond the included hotel breakfast, optional airline purchases, and any hotel incidental hold.
Is the $810.87 charged now, or at the hotel?

It is a pay-at-property rate. The card is used now to guarantee the reservation, but the room and tax are due at the hotel rather than prepaid. The property may place a temporary authorization for room, tax, and incidentals at check-in, so that authorization could be higher than $810.87 even though the quoted lodging charge is $810.87.
Spell out the cancellation deadline and what happens after it. The wording on hotel rates is easy to misread.

Free cancellation runs through Sunday, October 12 at 11:59 p.m. in the hotel's local time zone, which is Eastern Time. Canceling by that point avoids a room penalty.

A cancellation after the deadline, or a no-show, can incur a charge of the first night's room and tax. At the quoted rate, that is approximately $202.72. The remaining nights are not prepaid, but the exact penalty displayed in the final booking review controls.
So the flight is the more restrictive piece because it comes back as credit rather than a card refund?

Correct. Outside the 24-hour risk-free period, voluntarily canceling this Main Cabin fare would generally leave an airline eCredit, subject to the ticket's validity rules, instead of producing a cash refund to the corporate card. A change can also require additional payment if the replacement flight costs more.

The hotel is more flexible until 11:59 p.m. Eastern on October 12, after which the first-night penalty applies.
What about the Friday return? The client says we should finish by 3:30 in Cary. Is 5:35 from RDU realistic?

Yes, but the handoff should end on time. Leaving Cary around 3:40 to 3:50 p.m. would ordinarily put you at RDU around 4:10 to 4:30, depending on traffic. With no checked bag, that leaves roughly 65 to 85 minutes before the 5:35 departure.

If the work runs past about 4:00, the margin becomes thin. The itinerary is workable based on the stated 3:30 finish, but it does not provide much room for a significantly extended client session.
Keep that return. Can you confirm the hotel dates don't accidentally leave me checking out Thursday, and that late Monday arrival won't cancel the room?

The hotel stay is correctly set for check-in Monday, October 13 and check-out Friday, October 17: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday nights, four nights total.

A 10:38 p.m. flight arrival is within the hotel's normal late-arrival handling, but the reservation should carry an estimated arrival note of approximately 11:30 p.m. Because the room is card-guaranteed, it should be held overnight. If the flight is severely delayed past midnight, calling the property remains prudent so the reservation is not treated as a no-show.
Add the 11:30 p.m. arrival note. I have my traveler profile and corporate card ready. Give me one final purchase summary, including anything I need to explicitly accept.

Purchase-ready summary:

Delta Main Cabin, one traveler, round trip and nonstop. Depart MSP Monday, October 13 at 7:05 p.m.; arrive RDU at 10:38 p.m. Return Friday, October 17 at 5:35 p.m.; arrive MSP at 7:24 p.m. Airfare: $548 including taxes. One carry-on and one personal item are included; no checked bag is included. The fare is nonrefundable, changes may require a fare difference, and voluntary cancellation after the 24-hour risk-free period generally returns value as an eCredit rather than a card refund.

Hampton Inn & Suites Raleigh/Cary-I-40, standard king, check-in October 13 and check-out October 17, four nights. Room subtotal: $716. Estimated tax: $94.87. Hotel total: $810.87, payable at the property with the card used to guarantee the room. Free cancellation ends Sunday, October 12 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern; afterward, the estimated first-night penalty is $202.72. The reservation will note an approximately 11:30 p.m. arrival.

Combined flight and hotel: $1,358.87. Rideshares, incidentals, and optional airline charges are excluded. Both selections are ready for purchase with the stored traveler details and corporate card, but no charge has been submitted yet. Final authorization would mean accepting the airline's nonrefundability and eCredit terms, the hotel's post-deadline penalty, and the quoted totals subject to a last availability check.
